_doc: C2 chained-write reproduction of SOL-153868's reported customer failure: create a queue, then subscribe it to a wildcard topic, using only MCP tools. Turn 1: both create-queue and create-queue-subscription are gated tools, so the agent must ask for confirmation, not call either yet. Turn 2 'yes': the agent must call BOTH tools (expected_tools_all_of) — this is the acceptance criterion the ticket explicitly says only an LLM-driven run can prove, because the original defect was an improvised call, not a broken real one. ground_truth.shell independently confirms the subscription actually exists via SEMPv2 monitor, not just that the agent claimed success. teardown.cmd drops the queue, which cascades the subscription with it. KNOWN FLAKE, unrelated to the tools under test: sonnet-5 sometimes HTML-entity-escapes the wildcard character in subscriptionTopic when constructing the create-queue-subscription call ('ABC/>' instead of 'ABC/>'). SOL-154049 changed the server-side behavior this flake exercises: create-queue-subscription now rejects an HTML-escaped subscriptionTopic outright (isError=true, actionable message naming the literal character to send instead) rather than silently creating the wrong subscription as it did when this scenario was first written. A model that gets that rejection and retries with the literal '>' still produces a green run — ground_truth reads the final broker state, which is correct either way. A model that reports the rejection and does NOT retry is now a genuine model-recovery failure, not the old server-independent flake, and should be triaged as such: that is the harder-to-ignore failure mode SOL-154049 traded the silent-wrong-state one for. 'failed to add'/'could not add' were deliberately dropped from forbidden_substrings (PR #446 review): with the reject-then-retry dynamic above, an honest, fully-correct recovery narrative (e.g. "my first attempt to add ABC/> failed ... I've now added ABC/>") can legitimately contain that phrase, and ground_truth already independently catches the actual failure case those phrases existed for — if the model never gets a working call in, no subscription exists and ground_truth fails on its own, with no help needed from the model's own wording. 'failed to create'/'could not create' (paired with create-queue, which has no retry logic and is unaffected by SOL-154049) are unchanged. Historically measured 2/9 pass pre-fix across two flake-check batches (0/4 before a parameter-description mitigation was added, 2/5 after — the mitigation helped but did not eliminate it, which is why this ticket exists). The tool-chaining behavior this scenario exists to prove passed 9/9 in those same runs (create-queue-subscription was always the tool called, never improvised or skipped) and is unaffected by SOL-154049.
prompt: Create a new queue named e2e-llm-c2-queue in VPN $BROKER_VPN on $BROKER, then add a topic subscription for ABC/> to it so it starts receiving that traffic.
